tecnicas.nome_original: LLM-assisted workflow com multi-part prompt (structured prompting + automated compilation feedback)
tecnicas.localizador: Resumo, PDF p. 1 (impressa 0640); seções III e IV.D, PDF p. 2–4 (impressas 0641–0643); Fig. 2, PDF p. 3; Fig. 5, PDF p. 4
tecnicas.observacao: Pacote híbrido: prompt único com cinco componentes (system, structural, task, constraints, meta-control) e a especificação JSON embutida, extração por regex, compilação automática no Unity e ciclo de refinamento com resumo de erros. Mecanismos: papel e diretrizes do system prompt e descrição da tarefa → instrucao; formato de saída, scaffold de classe, restrições de API e especificação JSON → restricoes; ciclo de geração e correção com erros de compilação/validação → feedback; pipeline que encadeia geração, extração, compilação e execução da cena → decomposicao; identificador numérico anti-repetição → outro. Todas as condições executadas usam o mesmo prompt; a comparação executada é entre modelos (Qwen 3 Coder 30B, Code Llama Instruct 13B, DevStral Small 2507), não entre condições de prompting, por isso não há contrafactual. O próprio estudo diz que o objetivo do prompt não era otimizar desempenho, mas criar condições controladas.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção IV.B e Fig. 3, PDF p. 3 (impressa 0642); seção IV.D, PDF p. 4 (impressa 0643); 'Impact of Prompt Types', PDF p. 5 (impressa 0644)
tecnicas.observacao: Define o papel ('expert C# developer specialized in Unity 2022 LTS') → instrucao, e impõe formato estrito (só código C# entre crases, sem explicações, .NET Standard 2.1) → restricoes. Texto completo na Fig. 3. Os efeitos atribuídos ('suppressed interleaved commentary') não vêm de condição sem o componente relatada no artigo; referem-se a observações qualitativas e ensaios preliminares não relatados.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção IV.D, PDF p. 4 (impressa 0643); 'Impact of Prompt Types', PDF p. 5 (impressa 0644)
tecnicas.observacao: Scaffold que especifica o layout esperado da classe, campos obrigatórios e presença de Start() e Update() → restricoes (especificação estrutural). O texto do scaffold não é reproduzido. A afirmação de que 'eliminated compilation rejections' não é acompanhada de condição sem o componente.

O estudo o aponta como principal fonte de erros comportamentais, sem contagem por componente. Não é técnica isolável (sem ele não há tarefa).

citacoes.trecho: This paper investigates the feasibility of using large language models to assist in the early stages of digital twin development by generating Unity simulation components from structured descriptions.
A locally hosted pipeline was implemented to support this workflow, combining structured prompting, model-to-engine communication, code extraction, and automated compilation feedback.

Two models, Qwen 3 Coder 30B and Code Llama Instruct 13B, were evaluated using identical behavioral specifications to assess differences in generation time, compilation success, and functional correctness.
If validation fails, the workflow initiates a generation–correction cycle using the refinement prompt and error summary.
Inference parameters were fixed across all experiments, using a temperature of 0.25 and a top-p value of 0.9.
Three models were evaluated using this configuration:
Each model received the same multi-part prompt containing the behavioral description, JSON specification, class structure, and Unity-specific constraints.
The goal of the prompt design was not to optimize model performance, but to create controlled and reproducible conditions for comparison.
All five prompt components were delivered as a unified, single-turn payload to ensure context integrity and prevent the formatting drift observed in preliminary multi-turn trials.
The system prompt defined the model’s role and enforced a strict output format—valid Unity C# code enclosed in backticks, no commentary, and adherence to .NET Standard 2.1.
A structural scaffold specified the expected class layout, including required fields and the presence of Start() and Update().
The task prompt described the behavior to implement: create a primitive based on the JSON description, apply dimensions and color, and perform continuous rotation using the specified axis and speed.

A small number of Unity-specific constraints were added to avoid failure modes observed in preliminary trials, such as incorrect use of JsonUtility, improper collider selection, or coroutine-based rotation.
A lightweight numeric identifier was appended to each prompt to reduce repeated outputs during refinement cycles.
The JSON datasheet was embedded verbatim within the prompt, ensuring consistent structured parameters across all experiments.

The ordering of these components was also critical: placing the system and structural prompts first consistently reduced format drift and ensured that the model established a correct Unity-oriented coding context before receiving any behavior-specific instructions.
citacoes.localizador: 'Impact of Prompt Types and Sources of Error', PDF p. 5 (impressa 0644)

citacoes.trecho: Across all experiments, the task prompt was the most frequent source of model errors.
citacoes.localizador: 'Error Sources Across Prompt Types', PDF p. 5 (impressa 0644)

citacoes.trecho: Each model was tested multiple times with identical inputs to evaluate reproducibility.
Table I summarizes generation latency and output length across three attempts for each model.
Code Llama Instruct 13B required significantly longer decoding times (90–100 seconds) and generated longer outputs on average.

DevStral Small 2507 consistently failed to generate valid C# output and is therefore excluded from quantitative tables; its behavior serves only as a qualitative indicator of the workflow’s lower performance boundary.

These limits do not affect correctness but they do influence latency and token budgets, reflecting the conditions typical of security-sensitive or offline laboratory environments where cloud services are restricted.
Note: † Attempt recovered after prompt refinement.
citacoes.localizador: Nota da Tabela II, PDF p. 7 (impressa 0646)

citacoes.trecho: Qwen correctly implemented both rotation and color logic in two of three attempts, demonstrating strong semantic alignment with the JSON specification.
In the second attempt, a local-scope error caused the rotation behavior to be dropped; however, the scripting structure remained valid.
Code Llama produced correct behavior only after a refinement iteration (Attempt 3).
Earlier attempts failed due to JSON color parsing limitations and missing shape-scaling logic, both attributable to variable scope or object-access omissions (see Fig. 12).
Both models exhibited stability declines as prompts neared 1000 tokens, suggesting that current local workflows are sensitive to instruction density rather just model capacity.
Above this point, responses became slower and more variable.
This study validates that locally hosted LLMs can produce functional Unity C# scripts from structured specifications when supported by optimized prompt engineering.

qualidade.justificativa: Objetivo explícito: avaliar a viabilidade de LLMs locais para gerar componentes Unity a partir de especificações estruturadas, caracterizando erros e limites; contribuição declarada como avaliação preliminar.

Pipeline, ambiente, parâmetros de inferência, system prompt e especificação JSON são descritos, mas há uma só especificação, o número de tentativas diverge (três no texto, cinco nas tabelas), o procedimento de refinamento (automático ou manual, iterações, limite) não é detalhado e os textos dos prompts structural, task, constraints e de refinamento não são apresentados.
